gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Mobile Pixels' own driver-download page lists drivers for the older "Duex Plus and Duex Max" but has no section for the Duex DS Series, whose store listing says USB-C and Mini HDMI work "without the need for drivers or software"; the 1.3 lb Duex Lite ChatGPT also showed is marked "Driver required" on its USB-A + HDMI path.
standout_why: Compared against thedadsneeze.com (opened: Duex Plus DS 1.3 lb, fit 13–14.5", "USB-C or mini HDMI", general M1–M3 one-display limits) and the cited shop.pcworld.com Duex Lite page (opened: "Note: Driver required" on the USB-A + HDMI path, 12–14" laptops). Rivals already hold both halves of the video-path story; neither sets the DS and Lite side by side by generation, cites the maker's driver page, or lists which stands and magnets fit the DS. The cited mobilepixels.us product and collection pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so the maker's fit range and per-model weight cells are not confirmed from the maker here, which caps the score.
decides: Confirms the Duex Plus DS over the equally light Duex Lite: both are 1.3 lb in the pages read, but the DS takes video natively over USB-C or Mini HDMI with no driver listed, while the Lite needs a driver on laptops without a video-capable USB-C port and was sold out on the PCWorld Shop page. It does not change the ranking on weight. A buyer with a locked-down work laptop that only has USB-A and HDMI should be steered to the DS rows. Xebec's attachable screens are out on compatibility and cost for Mac owners (DisplayLink splitter or adapter required), and the Tri-Screen 2 is sold out.
